Introduction and meaning
Sexual harassment (old 354A): unwelcome physical contact and advances; a demand or request for sexual favours; showing pornography against her will; sexually coloured remarks. Remarks are the lighter band.
In student language: BNS s. 75 is the rule on “Sexual harassment”. The section provides that (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 75 exists so that “Sexual harassment” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
75. (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—

(i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or

(ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or

(iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or

(iv) making sexually coloured remarks,

shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment

(2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (i) or clause (ii) or clause (iii) of sub-section (1) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both

(3) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (iv) of sub-section (1) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 75 (Sexual harassment) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 75 (Sexual harassment), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) A man committing any of the following acts:—
   (2) (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or
   (3) (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or
   (4) (iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or
   (5) (iv) making sexually coloured remarks,
   (6) shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment
   (7) (2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause
   (8) (1) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 75 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 75 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Distinction. Contrast BNS s. 75 with BNS s. 74, BNS s. 79. Write a short table in prose: meaning, ingredients, stage of the case, consequence. Confusion of neighbouring sections is the most common reason arguments collapse under judicial scrutiny.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 75.”

learningObjectives: Understand the four statutory clauses defining sexual harassment under BNS s. 75.
Analyze the distinct penalties: up to three years for physical/verbal overtures, demands, and pornography; up to one year for sexually coloured remarks.
Distinguish sexual harassment from general assault under s. 74.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 75 defines sexual harassment as a man committing any of the following acts: (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or (iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or (iv) making sexually coloured remarks. Punishment: Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (i) or clause (ii) or clause (iii) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; any man who commits the offence specified in clause (iv) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Sexual harassment constitutes an actionable penal wrong safeguarding women from hostile, sexually coercive, or sexually offensive behavior in workplace, educational, and public environments.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 75 (corresponding to IPC s. 354A).
Clause (i): Unwelcome physical contact and explicit sexual advances.
Clause (ii): Demand or request for sexual favours.
Clause (iii): Showing pornography against her will.
Two-tier penalty: Clauses (i)-(iii) = RI up to 3 years or fine or both; Clause (iv) = Up to 1 year or fine or both.
essentialIngredients: The accused committed any of the four enumerated acts against a woman.
The conduct was unwelcome and of a sexual nature.
Penalty corresponds to the specific clause breached (3 years for i-iii, 1 year for iv).
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 75 codifies sexual harassment as a distinct penal crime. Unlike s. 74 (which requires criminal force or assault), s. 75 covers non-assaultive verbal, visual, and quid pro quo sexual conduct. Demanding sexual favours in exchange for a grade or promotion falls directly under Clause (ii). Showing pornographic videos or images on a mobile phone to an unwilling female colleague falls under Clause (iii). Making lewd, sexually coloured remarks about a woman's body falls under Clause (iv). The section works alongside the POSH Act, providing the criminal penal sanction.
examples: Teaching example (Demand for sexual favours): A manager calls a female subordinate to his office and states that her contract will be terminated unless she agrees to spend the weekend with him at a hotel. Clause (ii) is violated; the manager faces up to 3 years RI.

Teaching example (Showing pornography): A coworker deliberately thrusts his smartphone displaying hardcore pornography in front of a female colleague despite her objections. Clause (iii) applies; up to 3 years RI.
Teaching example (Sexually coloured remarks): An accused repeatedly makes vulgar, sexually explicit remarks regarding a woman's anatomy in an elevator. Clause (iv) applies; up to 1 year imprisonment.
distinctions: Section 74 vs Section 75: Section 74 requires criminal force/assault with intent to outrage modesty; Section 75 penalizes unwelcome sexual overtures, demands, pornography, and remarks even without assault.
Clause (i)-(iii) vs Clause (iv): Physical advances, demands, and pornography carry 3 years RI; verbal sexually coloured remarks carry 1 year.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a supervisor who repeatedly forwarded sexually explicit video clips to an unwilling female subordinate can be prosecuted under BNS s. 75.
Rule: Under BNS s. 75(1)(iii), showing pornography against the will of a woman constitutes sexual harassment punishable with up to three years imprisonment.
Application: Digital transmission of pornographic clips against her express protests constitutes showing pornography against her will.
Conclusion: The supervisor is guilty under s. 75(1)(iii).

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 75 four clauses of sexual harassment.
State the two penalty tiers: up to 3 years for (i)-(iii), up to 1 year for (iv).
Highlight that it covers verbal demands and pornography.

keyTakeaways: Four specific forms: advances, demands, pornography, sexually coloured remarks.
Advances, demands, and pornography carry up to 3 years RI.
Sexually coloured remarks carry up to 1 year imprisonment.
